name: International Protection (Proteção Internacional)

requirements.blocker_text: This can only be claimed while on Portuguese territory or at a border post — no applications from abroad.

This requires meeting one of two protection categories: refugee status (persecution under the Geneva Convention grounds) or subsidiary protection (risk of serious harm, including from war or generalized violence, if returned).

evidence_required.document: Evidence supporting the persecution or serious-harm claim
Attendance at AIMA/CNAR screening and interview

outcome.duration_length: refugee status: 5 years, renewable; subsidiary protection: 3 years, renewable subject to country-of-origin reassessment

sources.title: Diário da República — Lei n.º 27/2008 (Asylum Law) and Constitution Art. 33

notes: No application fee, same as every other country's asylum route in this dataset. Two protection statuses with genuinely different durations (refugee: 5 years; subsidiary: 3 years, subject to a country-of-origin safety re-examination at renewal) — same structural pattern as Germany's asylum route, modeled as a single group for the same reason (the schema can't cleanly express 'either of two tests with different downstream durations' without fragmenting the route). Statutory decision target ~6 months, but this figure should be read against the AIMA backlog context documented across every other Portugal route in this dataset — asylum claims specifically compete for the same overwhelmed processing capacity, and realistic timelines are likely to exceed the statutory target by a wide margin, though this wasn't independently quantified for asylum specifically during this research pass. Dublin Regulation transfers apply, same EU-wide mechanic relevant to all Schengen-area asylum routes, not separately modeled as a requirement here.
